$comment: Cross-language contract for tenant resource naming. `lib/rust/tenant-auth` — which the three proxies route with — and `lib/typescript/services`, which creates the databases and roles, MUST both produce these exact strings. A divergence is a security bug: the control plane creates one database and the proxy connects a tenant to another, or to nothing. AGENTS.md names this as one of three contracts with shared vectors; it was the one with none, and the two sides had drifted. TypeScript built names from the raw UUID hex, Rust from the Crockford short id, and each language asserted its own answer in its own test. `keyPrefix` was added later, for the same reason the rest of the file exists. The Valkey key prefix is built in three places — `keyspace::prefix_for` in the proxy, `tenantQueuePrefix` in `@lib/queue`, and `tenantKeyPrefix` in `@lib/reaper` — and had no shared vector. The proxy writes every tenant key under it and the reaper deletes by it, so a divergence is not a cosmetic bug: the reaper matches nothing, reports success, and a deleted customer's data stays in the shared instance forever.

cases.note: the vector the Rust crate already asserted, and the one TypeScript did not produce
the service provisioned on the live cluster, whose database TypeScript named sprout_db_01a022cb93bf74f9969791423c4b0b72 — 32 hex characters the proxy would never look for
a second kind: the username prefix changes, the short id does not
